value: mostly crepuscular with some diurnal activity; more nocturnal during the breeding period
method: remote camera traps (120 cameras, 12 per locality, 40-60 cm above ground, running 24 h, three images per trigger with 1 s delay); lynx activity overlap with genet and stone marten estimated from detection times
conditions: Free-ranging Iberian lynx in Sierra de Andujar Natural Park, southern Spain; camera-trapping survey between October and May of 2018-19 and 2019-20 in ten localities (five with territorial lynx presence, five outside the lynx range as controls; lynx detections come from the five lynx localities within the one park; 156 independent adult lynx captures in total, 2.30 +/- 0.56 per 100 camera-days). The paper's breeding period is the denning period from March to June; lynx activity is reported as mostly crepuscular outside it and turning more nocturnal during it, so the value carries both parts. No lynx-specific sex or individual difference is reported. Genet and stone marten activity in the same paper (strictly nocturnal, one sentence for both species) is not filed here.
